Autonomy.description:
How much an agent may do about a problem, without being told.

ALERT     report it; no command exists that fixes it unattended
APPROVE   a command exists, and a human authorises it before it runs
AUTO      narrow, reversible, auditable -- safe to run unattended

FAIL CLOSED: a problem with no explicit tier is ALERT. The guidance is
explicit that a system should "fail closed when risk classification,
approval validation, policy lookup, or audit logging fails".
Autonomy.title: Autonomy

ContractProblem.description:
One thing wrong, in a form both an agent and a person can use.

MOVED HERE FROM nix_contract, because a problem IS a code plus a message
plus a Remediation -- it belongs beside the thing it carries. Leaving it in
nix_contract would have forced an import cycle the moment nix_output needed
to type its `problems` field.
ContractProblem.title: ContractProblem

ProbeRecord.description:
One command this contract ran, and what it did.

WHY EVERY PROBE IS RECORDED, INCLUDING THE ONES THAT SUCCEEDED
A contract that reports only conclusions cannot be audited. With this, a
reader can see WHICH commands produced the verdict -- and a slow success
("`nix eval` took 30s") is a signal a boolean cannot carry.

TRUNCATION IS EVIDENCE, NOT SILENCE
`truncated` is recorded rather than left implicit, so a reader can tell a
short error from a cut one. A production runner names this requirement
exactly: "bounded stdout/stderr capture WITH TRUNCATION EVIDENCE".

ARGV IS RECORDED, AND THAT IS SAFE HERE SPECIFICALLY
Argument redaction matters wherever a command receives a secret. These are
fixed `nix` invocations with store paths, run in an environment CONSTRUCTED
rather than inherited -- nothing sensitive is passed in to echo back. That
reasoning does not survive a command taking a credential as an argument, and
redaction must come first if one is ever added.

Remediation.description:
What to do about a problem, in a form an agent can act on.

command IS NOT RUN BY THIS PROGRAM. It is a proposal. The separation is the
point: this module decides, something else executes, and the something else
is gated by `autonomy`.
